stem: A new customer hasn't purchased a support plan.
prompt: What support does it still receive?

options.text: The full set of Trusted Advisor checks in every category
options.why: Basic includes only core checks, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.

options.text: 24/7 phone access to Cloud Support Engineers for technical issues
options.why: Phone access requires a paid plan such as Business.

options.text: Billing help, documentation, re:Post and the Health Dashboard
options.why: Basic Support includes these for all customers.

options.text: A designated Technical Account Manager for proactive guidance
options.why: TAMs come with Enterprise-level plans, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.

explanation.answer: AWS Basic Support is included for all customers: account and billing help, documentation, whitepapers, re:Post, AWS Health Dashboard and core Trusted Advisor checks.
explanation.concept: Paid plans add technical support from engineers.
explanation.examTip: No plan = Basic: billing help, docs, re:Post, Health Dashboard, core Trusted Advisor.

stem: A startup is experimenting on AWS and wants business-hours email access to technical support at the lowest cost.

options.why: Enterprise is designed for business-critical workloads and costs much more.
Business adds 24/7 phone and chat, at higher cost.
Basic doesn't include technical support cases.
Developer Support offers business-hours email access to Cloud Support Associates.

explanation.answer: AWS Developer Support suits experimenting or testing on AWS, with business-hours web/email access to technical support.
explanation.concept: Business and higher add 24/7 access and faster response times.
explanation.examTip: Testing/experimenting + cheapest technical support = Developer.

stem: A company runs production workloads and needs 24/7 phone, email and chat access to Cloud Support Engineers plus the full set of Trusted Advisor checks.
prompt: Which is the LOWEST-cost plan that meets this?

options.why: Business Support includes 24/7 access to engineers and full Trusted Advisor checks.
Basic doesn't include technical support access.
Enterprise meets the needs but costs more than required.
Developer offers business-hours email only.

explanation.answer: AWS Business Support is recommended for production workloads and includes 24/7 technical support and the full set of Trusted Advisor checks.
explanation.concept: It also includes AWS Health API access.
explanation.examTip: Production + 24/7 phone + full Trusted Advisor (lowest cost) = Business.

stem: A large company runs mission-critical workloads and wants a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM) who knows its environment.
prompt: Which support plan includes a designated TAM?

options.why: Developer doesn't include a TAM, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
Enterprise Support includes a designated TAM.
Business doesn't include a TAM, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
On-Ramp provides access to a pool of TAMs, not a designated one.

explanation.answer: AWS Enterprise Support includes a designated Technical Account Manager who provides proactive guidance and advocacy.
explanation.concept: Enterprise On-Ramp includes a pool of TAMs.
explanation.examTip: Designated TAM = Enterprise. Pool of TAMs = Enterprise On-Ramp.

stem: A company wants a dedicated team to help with billing and account questions, such as invoices and account best practices, as part of its support plan.

options.why: Trusted Advisor gives automated recommendations.
Professional Services delivers consulting engagements.
The Concierge team helps with billing and account questions for Enterprise On-Ramp and Enterprise customers.
re:Post is community Q&A, so it doesn't meet this requirement.

explanation.answer: The Concierge Support Team, included with Enterprise On-Ramp and Enterprise Support, specializes in billing and account inquiries.
explanation.concept: TAMs focus on technical guidance; Concierge focuses on billing and account.
explanation.examTip: Billing and account experts = Concierge (Enterprise-level plans).

stem: A company on Developer Support wants all Trusted Advisor checks, including cost optimization checks.

options.why: Config doesn't unlock Trusted Advisor checks.
Purchases don't change Trusted Advisor access.

options.text: Stay on Developer, which already includes every check
options.why: Developer Support includes only the core Trusted Advisor checks.

options.text: Upgrade to Business Support or higher
options.why: Full Trusted Advisor checks come with Business, Enterprise On-Ramp and Enterprise.

explanation.answer: Basic and Developer include core Trusted Advisor checks. Business Support and higher include the full set of checks.
explanation.concept: Trusted Advisor categories: cost optimization, performance, security, fault tolerance, service limits and operational excellence.
explanation.examTip: Full Trusted Advisor = Business or higher.

stem: A company wants automated recommendations on cost savings, security, fault tolerance, performance and service quotas.

options.why: Trusted Advisor checks accounts against AWS best practices across these categories.
Artifact provides compliance reports, which isn't what this scenario needs.
CloudTrail logs API calls, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
Inspector focuses on vulnerabilities, so it doesn't meet this requirement.

explanation.answer: AWS Trusted Advisor evaluates your account and recommends improvements for cost, performance, security, fault tolerance, service limits and operational excellence.
explanation.concept: Check results show red, yellow or green status.
explanation.examTip: Best-practice checks across categories = Trusted Advisor.

stem: An administrator wants to know about upcoming AWS maintenance that will affect specific EC2 instances.

options.why: Budgets track spending, which isn't what this scenario needs.
The Health Dashboard shows events and scheduled changes affecting your resources.
Marketplace sells software, which isn't what this scenario needs.
This estimates costs, so it doesn't meet this requirement.

explanation.answer: The AWS Health Dashboard provides personalized information about events that affect your AWS resources, including scheduled maintenance.
explanation.concept: It's available to all customers.
explanation.examTip: Events affecting my resources = AWS Health Dashboard.

stem: A developer has a technical question and wants answers from the AWS community and experts without opening a support case.

options.why: Artifact provides compliance reports, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Budgets track cost, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
re:Post is a community Q&A site with AWS experts.
Organizations manages accounts, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.

explanation.answer: AWS re:Post is a free, community-driven Q&A service for AWS questions.
explanation.concept: Questions may be answered by community members, AWS employees and AWS experts.
explanation.examTip: Free community answers = re:Post.

stem: A company wants AWS experts to work alongside its team to deliver a large migration project.

options.why: re:Post is community Q&A, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
The Free Tier offers free usage, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
Trusted Advisor gives automated checks, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Professional Services is a team of experts that helps customers achieve business outcomes on AWS.

explanation.answer: AWS Professional Services provides experts who work with customers and partners on migrations, modernization and other projects.
explanation.concept: AWS Partners also provide consulting and implementation services.
explanation.examTip: AWS experts on your project = Professional Services (or AWS Partners).

stem: A company wants to find a certified consulting firm to help build its AWS environment.

options.text: The AWS Partner Network (Partner Solutions Finder)
options.why: The AWS Partner Network lists validated consulting and technology partners.

options.text: AWS Marketplace, under the AMI and SaaS listings
options.why: Marketplace sells software and some services, but the Partner Network is where you find validated consulting partners.

options.text: AWS re:Post, by asking for consultant referrals
options.why: re:Post is community Q&A, not a directory of validated partners.

options.text: AWS Artifact, under the third-party reports section
options.why: Artifact provides compliance reports, which isn't what this scenario needs.

explanation.answer: The AWS Partner Network (APN) is a global community of partners that offer consulting services and software solutions on AWS.
explanation.concept: Partners can earn competencies that validate expertise in specific areas.
explanation.examTip: Find consulting/technology partners = AWS Partner Network.

stem: A company wants to buy a third-party monitoring tool that runs on AWS, with charges on its AWS bill.

options.why: This estimates AWS costs, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Marketplace offers third-party software billed through AWS.
Trusted Advisor gives recommendations, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Service Catalog lists your organization's approved products.

explanation.answer: AWS Marketplace is a digital catalog of third-party software, data and services that run on AWS, with flexible pricing and AWS billing.
explanation.concept: Products include SaaS, AMIs, containers and professional services.
explanation.examTip: Buy third-party software through AWS = Marketplace.

stem: A company's business-critical system is down. It wants the fastest AWS Support response time available.
prompt: Which plan offers the fastest response for this case?

options.why: Basic doesn't include technical support cases.
Developer response times are measured in hours and business hours only.
Enterprise Support offers the fastest response for business-critical system down cases.
Business offers fast responses for production outages but not the fastest.

explanation.answer: AWS Enterprise Support offers the fastest response times for business-critical system outages, along with a designated TAM.
explanation.concept: Response times improve at each higher support tier.
explanation.examTip: Fastest response for critical outages = Enterprise.

stem: A retailer is preparing for Black Friday and wants AWS experts to help plan and monitor its infrastructure during the event.

options.text: A Savings Plan sized for the expected peak
options.why: Savings Plans lower prices; they don't provide expert event planning.

options.text: AWS Trusted Advisor service limit checks
options.why: Trusted Advisor flags quota issues but doesn't plan or monitor an event with you.

options.text: An AWS Well-Architected review in the console
options.why: A Well-Architected review assesses a workload but doesn't provide event-day planning and monitoring support.
Infrastructure Event Management helps plan and run large events.

explanation.answer: Infrastructure Event Management provides architecture and scaling guidance and operational support during planned events like launches and sales.
explanation.concept: It's included with Enterprise Support and available with other plans for a fee.
explanation.examTip: Big planned event + AWS help = Infrastructure Event Management.

stem: A new user wants official step-by-step guides and API references for AWS services.

options.why: AWS documentation provides user guides, tutorials and API references.
Marketplace sells third-party products, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
Budgets track cost, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
The Health Dashboard shows service events.

explanation.answer: AWS documentation includes user guides, developer guides, API references and tutorials for every service.
explanation.concept: Whitepapers and the Well-Architected Framework provide broader guidance.
explanation.examTip: How to use a service = AWS documentation.

stem: A company is comparing AWS Support plans.
prompt: Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: All plans include the AWS Health Dashboard
options.why: Health Dashboard access is included with Basic and above.

options.text: Basic includes 24/7 technical support by phone
options.why: Basic doesn't include technical support.

options.text: Business Support includes 24/7 phone access to engineers
options.why: Business provides 24/7 phone, email and chat.

options.text: Developer includes a designated Technical Account Manager
options.why: TAMs come with Enterprise-level plans, which isn't what this scenario needs.

options.text: Enterprise On-Ramp includes a designated TAM
options.why: On-Ramp includes a pool of TAMs, not a designated one.

explanation.answer: Basic includes the Health Dashboard and core checks. Business adds 24/7 engineer access. Enterprise adds a designated TAM.
explanation.concept: Know which features first appear at which plan level.
explanation.examTip: 24/7 engineers start at Business; designated TAM only at Enterprise.

stem: A company wants architectural guidance from AWS for a new workload but isn't ready for a paid consulting engagement.

options.why: Trusted Advisor gives automated checks, not personalized architecture guidance.

options.text: AWS Solutions Architects via the account team
options.why: AWS Solutions Architects provide architectural guidance to customers.
The Health Dashboard reports service events, not design advice.
The SRT helps with DDoS events, not general architecture guidance.

explanation.answer: AWS Solutions Architects work with customers to provide technical guidance and best practices for designing workloads.
explanation.concept: Other resources include AWS Prescriptive Guidance, the Well-Architected Framework and AWS Partners.
explanation.examTip: Architecture advice from AWS = Solutions Architects (account team).

stem: A company on Business Support has a production issue with an EC2 instance.
prompt: How should it get help from AWS?

options.text: Post the issue on AWS re:Post and wait for answers
options.why: re:Post is community help; with Business Support, the company should open a case for a production issue.

options.text: Wait for the AWS Health Dashboard to resolve it
options.why: The Health Dashboard reports events; it doesn't fix customer issues.

options.text: Open a technical case in the AWS Support Center
options.why: Paid plans can open technical cases by web, phone or chat.

options.text: Ask the Concierge team, which handles technical issues
options.why: Concierge focuses on billing and account questions, and comes with Enterprise-level plans.

explanation.answer: Customers with paid plans can open technical support cases in the AWS Support Center console, choosing severity and contact method.
explanation.concept: Basic Support covers account and billing cases only.
explanation.examTip: Technical help = open a support case (paid plans).

stem: A team wants AWS-vetted strategies, guides and patterns for migrating and modernizing workloads.

options.why: Budgets track cost, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Trusted Advisor gives automated checks, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Artifact provides compliance reports, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
Prescriptive Guidance provides vetted strategies, guides and patterns.

explanation.answer: AWS Prescriptive Guidance offers time-tested strategies, guides and patterns from AWS and partners to accelerate cloud projects.
explanation.concept: It includes migration strategy guidance like the 7 Rs.
explanation.examTip: Vetted migration/modernization patterns = Prescriptive Guidance.

stem: A company wants to change its AWS Support plan.

options.text: The support plan can be changed in the AWS Support Center console
options.why: Customers can upgrade or change plans in the console.

options.text: Support plans are fixed for the first three years of an account
options.why: There's no such lock-in; plans can be changed.

options.text: Only AWS Professional Services can change plans
options.why: Customers change plans themselves, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.

options.text: The plan is chosen automatically based on spend
options.why: Customers choose their plan, so it doesn't meet this requirement.

explanation.answer: You can change your AWS Support plan in the console. Changing the support plan requires root user or appropriate IAM permissions.
explanation.concept: Paid plan fees are typically a percentage of monthly AWS usage, with a minimum.
explanation.examTip: Change support plan = Support Center console.
